newsitem.title: GERMANY: Schenker to open 50m mark Singapore hub.
newsitem.headline: Schenker to open 50m mark Singapore hub.

text.p: Global freight forwarder Schenker International AG said it will open a 50 million mark logistics hub in Singapore next January.
Schenker International logistics manager Reinhard Riss said the 25,000 square-metre freight centre would serve as the forwarder's storage and distribution base for the Asia-Pacific region.
The Asian market, and intra-Asian transport in particular, would be the major area of growth for freight transport over the next few years, Riss told Reuters in an interview.

Half of the Singapore logistics centre space has already been leased to existing clients such as Siemens AG and new customers including Volkswagen AG, Lufthansa catering arm LSG and Nokia Oy, he said.
"VW has rented 6,000 square metres on a long-term contract for its South-east Asia spare parts centre. The company wants to have its spare parts in the market within days and not in weeks," he said.
LSG would use the centre to supply passenger aircraft coming from the Far East with food and non-food products, Riss said.

The four-storey centre, with separate stores for valuable goods, perishables and hazardous goods, will go into operation towards the end of 1997, with the official opening set for next January, he added.
Riss said Schenker International planned to open further logistics hubs as part of developing a full range of services, including warehousing and supply chain management.
An existing centre in Shenzhen would be joined by new terminals in Shanghai and Beijing by 2000, he added.
A European logistics centre could open in the Netherlands and similar sites could also open on the east and west coasts of the United States by 2000.
